messages:
Jia Chen: Heads-up — our new GPU nodepool in ap-southeast-1 is failing to attach to the NLB: targets are being rejected. I think we've hit a target-group / VPCE quota. Can infra help with an increase?

Mike R.: Do you have the exact error/logs? Which quota is tripping?

Jia Chen: Error from controller:
```
E0321 14:02:11.123 controller.go:312] failed to register targets for service gpu-inference: Failed to register targets: TooManyTargets: The number of targets exceeds the quota for this account
status code: 400, request id: 8f3a-xxxx
```
Also seeing ENI attach failures when creating interface endpoints for the model-serving namespace.

Alex P.: Sounds like two related limits: (1) target groups / targets per region or per NLB, and (2) aws VPC endpoint (interface) quotas / ENI limits. We recently added more nodepools and each pod uses an IP target. Suggest we request increases for both: Target Groups per NLB and Interface Endpoints per VPC.

Tara S.: +1. Please open an AWS support ticket with exact quota ids and desired values. @infra-bot can you create the ticket and add the details from Jia? Include a justification: prod traffic growth + new GPU clusters for customer D. Also propose alternate/fallback plan. :thumbsup:

Jia Chen: Created a draft in the ticket form:
- Service: Elastic Load Balancing (elasticloadbalancing)
- Quota: Target groups per region / per account (we're currently at ~60 TGs)
- Request: increase to 300 target groups in ap-southeast-1
- Service: VPC Endpoints (vpce) - Interface endpoints per VPC
- Request: increase from 50 to 200
Justification: onboarding 3 GPU-backed clusters for latency-sensitive customers; short-term spike expected.

infra-bot: AWS Support case created: case-2026-03-21-0001. Assigned priority: normal. Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=case-2026-03-21-0001

Mike R.: Thanks. What's the rollback / mitigation if AWS takes days? We can't have new nodes stuck.

Alex P.: Mitigation options:
- Temporarily scale new nodepool size down and route traffic to existing clusters.
- Switch to IP-mode where possible (reuse existing target groups) or consolidate services to fewer TGs.
- Create a separate VPC for heavy-GPU workloads if interface endpoints per VPC is the bottleneck (longer-term).

Jia Chen: Implemented quick workaround: disabled automatic nodepool autoscaler for the new pool and started a scaled-down pool (2 nodes) so no new target registration attempts. Logging it here so we can re-enable once quota approved.

Tara S.: Please add the case id to the monthly quota-change tracker and tag the affected clusters and services (team:infra, purpose:gpu-onboarding). I'll follow up with AWS if we don't hear back in 48h.

Alex P.: I'll update the runbook with the mitigation steps and the recommended target numbers. Also adding notes about cost impact (more TGs and endpoints = slight extra fees).

Jia Chen: Thanks all — will post update when case moves. If AWS approves, we'll plan a controlled re-enable and monitor connection errors closely. :eyes:
